purpose: Close ASVS V15.3.7 (parameter pollution) for the cookie source. The web tier resolved one Cookie header two ways: readCookie in server-request-security.ts, which assertCsrf uses, and the equivalent reader in server-request-actor.ts took the first occurrence of a name, while Next's RequestCookies, used by staff/open-cabinet, keeps the last because it builds a map by name. For a header carrying a name twice, the deciding value depended on which route was called. A second, related defect in the same reader: decodeURIComponent throws URIError on a value such as '%' or '%zz', and the exception left assertCsrf, so a request with a malformed cookie got 500 instead of 403. The fix is one shared reader that returns an empty value when a name is ambiguous or undecodable, so every caller refuses rather than picks a side. Extracted unchanged from PR #5102, where it was measured, so that it can be reviewed on its own.
requiredInvariants: A request that carries each cookie name once is handled exactly as before: same value, same CSRF and session outcome.

The platform cannot produce the ambiguous case itself: every Set-Cookie for the CSRF and access cookies, server-side and in the demo client script, is host-only with Path=/, so a repeat overwrites rather than adds. A repeated name therefore comes from another origin under the same registrable domain, and it is refused, not resolved.
Origin checks, token comparison, cookie attributes and session handling are unchanged; only how the Cookie header is read changes.
The shared reader never throws; an undecodable value is treated as absent.
New test files are wired into the CI-gated web-unit step, not added to the exclusion registry.
The cryptographic inventory is regenerated by scripts/security/discover-cryptography.mjs, never edited by hand.
No migration, schema, dependency, lockfile or production configuration change.
Merge and CI success are not REG.RU production deployment evidence.

Behaviour change on staff/open-cabinet. On main that route accepted a CSRF token that matched any value Next returned for the name. It now refuses when the name is repeated. A legitimate browser session never repeats it, per the invariant above; confirm that no deployment sets pc_csrf_token with a Domain attribute.
acceptance: The two former readers are measured to disagree on a repeated cookie name, and the shared reader refuses that header instead.
assertCsrf and staff/open-cabinet both refuse a duplicated CSRF cookie, whichever of its values the header matches, and both still accept a single matching cookie.
A malformed percent-encoding in the cookie yields a refusal, not an exception.
Exactly one file in apps/web reads the Cookie header directly.
